This isn't just in games, this happens in all industries. I'm guessing it's a result of poor project management. I've worked for a number of companies doing software development and this is how it usually goes.

  1. Management comes up with a project idea
  2. Management pulls a release date out of their ass without consulting anyone else
  3. Management scopes "everything" that they want to do (notice that they're figuring out the details after arriving at the schedule)
  4. Management finally lets everyone else know what they have already planned.
  5. Devs and project managers spend a lot of time trying to figure out WTF management actually wants and needs
  6. by the time development has a good enough grasp of what management wants they're already behind schedule
  7. Project management tries to push back the release date to a reasonable timeline (if you have a good PM)
  8. Devs show first demo. by now management has completely changed their direction and tells the devs to "fix" things
  9. Devs bitch and moan while "fixing" things to meet the new requirements
  10. By now they're way behind schedule so they need to start dropping features and rushing through sections of the project. Rushing through sections can often explain why the beginning of games start off great, but become boring and repetitive later.
  11. As the deadline comes closer management panics and starts having more meetings. this further slows down development time.
  12. major features are dropped and bugs are allowed to slide. "We'll fix it in the next release" becomes the teams mantra.
  13. The release date needs to be pushed back anyway.
  14. Finally, version 1.0 is released. it's full of bugs and missing features, but we can fix all that later right?
  15. management moves onto the next project and leaves a handful of demoralized devs to fix everything.

Not all companies are this bad. I've worked for a number of companies that did a great job managing their projects, but I'm guessing a lot of businesses follow this general path.

RANT WARNING: If you're management or a project manager: I understand that falling behind schedule is stressful and you're being pressured to provide info up the chain, but I can't stress enough how much you're harming the project by just arbitrarily calling status update meetings with your devs. Every interruption your devs have to address can result in hours of downtime (Beyond however long the meeting took) just trying to recover from the meeting and get back into their programming mindset.
